Sam Bhat: Quick sanity check — ran a 5k-sample perf sweep across us-east / us-west / eu-west with the new edge-split routing. Noticed a consistent p95 jump in eu-west that correlates with hop_count > 3 :thinking:

Sam Bhat: Test config (short):
```
perf_harness.py --model redwood-medium --gpu A10G --quant q8_0 --seq 1024 --concurrency 32 --duration 5m --edge-split 0.6 --route-policy edge-balanced --record-hops
```

Julia Kim: Can you paste the raw p50/p95 numbers and hop distribution? Also which kernel flags were active?

Sam Bhat: Raw excerpt (median of 3 runs):
```
region,gpu,p50_ms,p95_ms,avg_hops,notes
us-east,A10G,22,36,1.4,stable
us-west,A10G,24,39,1.6,stable
eu-west,A10G,28,94,3.8,p95 spike when hop>3
```

Rahul Desai: Interesting. I profiled the requests that hit eu-west. We saw an attention kernel fallback when seq_len > 768 — falls back from `attn_fused_v2` to `attn_generic` for some shard placements. That fallback multiplies per-token latency. Also RPC serialization increases with hop count.

Rahul Desai: Profiler snippet:
```
# profiler summary for slow trace
kernel.attn_fused_v2: 42% time
kernel.attn_generic: 48% time (used on slow traces)
rpc.serialize: 6% time (hop_count=4)
cpu.dequant: 3% time (proxy)
```

Marta Li: I ran the same harness but toggled quantization and proxy placement. q4_0 had worse tails in eu-west because the dequant step on the proxy CPU was single-threaded and saturated at high hop counts. Switching to q8_0 lowered p95 but increased p50 slightly. We also saw large improvements after enabling prefix KV caching for repeated prompts. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Marta Li: Numbers (eu-west comparison):
```
config,p50_ms,p95_ms
q4_0 + proxy-dequant,31,128
q8_0 + proxy-dequant,29,72
q8_0 + proxy-dequant + kv-cache,27,45
q8_0 + local-dequant,28,50
```

Sam Bhat: So two root causes: (1) kernel fallback on certain shard/hop placements, (2) CPU-side dequant on proxy when hop_count high. Both amplify tail latency.

Julia Kim: Do we have a quick mitigation path for customer impact? Can we route long-seq requests to lower-hop paths or prefer nodes with fused kernels?

Rahul Desai: Short-term: add a routing policy rule that prefers nodes advertising `attn_fused_v2=true` for seq_len >= 768 and prioritize low-hop paths for high-priority requests. Medium-term: upstream kernel fix and move dequant to multi-threaded path or offload to GPU proxy.

Sam Bhat: I pushed a canary routing tweak to staging that biases edge-split towards lower hop_count for long sequences. infra-bot: deploy log below.

infra-bot: [deploy] canary/edge-router v2025.11.3 -> staging at 2025-08-24T14:42:10Z :white_check_mark:

Marta Li: After the canary in staging I re-ran the harness, p95 in eu-west dropped to ~48ms with kv-cache enabled (closer to baseline). We should run a short A/B for 4 hours on production traffic.

Sam Bhat: Action items:
- Rahul: add an explicit kernel-capability tag to node metadata (attn_fused_v2 / attn_generic) and expose to router (owner: rahul) — ETA 2d
- Infra: add hop_count preference toggle to routing config for >seq_len 768 — ETA 1d (staging canary done)
- Marta: run 4h A/B on prod traffic for edge-split bias + kv-cache, collect p50/p95 and failure rate — ETA 4h after config flips
- Julia: update eval runbook with this pattern (hop_count + kernel fallback) and a checklist for onboarding new models with long seqs — ETA EOD

Julia Kim: Thanks — please paste links to the perf runs and canary dashboard when available.

Sam Bhat: Perf run artifacts: https://perf.redwood.example/runs/1748213476 (staging)
Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/edge-router/canary-1748213476

Marta Li: tagging @infra for prod toggle and @ops for A/B monitoring.

Rahul Desai: noted, will start the node-tag work today.

Sam Bhat: Closing loop later with post-A/B numbers. Thanks all :pray:
